```{r}

data <- read_excel("C:/Users/jx4634yi/Downloads/DATA 211 Final Project Data collections.xlsx")

# let us Rename columns
names(data)[1:4] <- c("Date", "Day", "Footsteps", "Calories_Burned")

# Converting  date into a good format
data$Date <- as.Date(
  gsub("_", " ", data$Date),
  format = "%B %d"
)

# using set up year of 2026 
data$Date <- as.Date(
  paste0("2026-", format(data$Date, "%m-%d"))
)

# variable for analysis
data <- data %>%
  select(Date, Day, Footsteps, Calories_Burned)

head(data)

```
# scatter plot 
```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Footsteps, y = Calories_Burned)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Daily Footsteps and Calories Burned",
    x = "Daily Footsteps (steps)",
    y = "Daily Calories Burned (calories)"
  ) +
  xlim(0,8000)+
  ylim(0,3500)+
  theme_minimal()
```

# LIne Graph of daily footstep 
```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Date, y = Footsteps)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Footsteps Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Daily Footsteps (steps)"
  ) +
  ylim(0,8000)+
  theme_minimal()



```


# Daily footstep and calories burned 
```{r}
# Scale factor for displaying both variables
scale_factor <- max(data$Footsteps, na.rm = TRUE) /
                max(data$Calories_Burned, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Date)) +
  # Daily footsteps (blue line)
  geom_line(aes(y = Footsteps, color = "Footsteps"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Footsteps, color = "Footsteps"),
             size = 2) +

  # Daily calories burned (red line)
  geom_line(aes(y = Calories_Burned * scale_factor,
                color = "Calories Burned"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Calories_Burned * scale_factor,
                 color = "Calories Burned"),
             size = 2) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Daily Footsteps (steps)",
    limits = c(0, 8000),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . / scale_factor,
      name = "Daily Calories Burned (calories)"
    )
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Footsteps" = "blue",
               "Calories Burned" = "red")
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Daily Footsteps and Calories Burned Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    color = "Variable"
  ) +

  theme_minimal()
```




# Historigram of dialy footsteps
```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Footsteps)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1000,
    fill = "skyblue",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Daily Footsteps",
    x = "Daily Footsteps (steps)",
    y = "Frequency (days)"
  ) +
  xlim(0,8000)+
  theme_minimal()
```


# historigram of dialy footstep and calories burned 
```{r}
# Histogram for daily footsteps
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Footsteps)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 1000,
    fill = "blue",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Footsteps",
    x = "Footsteps (steps)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 8000)) +
  theme_minimal()

# Histogram for daily calories burned
p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Calories_Burned)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 200,
    fill = "red",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Calories Burned",
    x = "Calories Burned (calories)",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 3500)) +
  theme_minimal()

# Display both histograms together
gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```



# combine both historigram together 

```{r}
# Combine the two variables
hist_data <- data.frame(
  Value = c(data$Footsteps, data$Calories_Burned),
  Variable = rep(
    c("Daily Footsteps", "Calories Burned"),
    each = nrow(data)
  )
)

# Create both histograms
ggplot(hist_data, aes(x = Value, fill = Variable)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 7,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Variable,
    scales = "free_x",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Daily Footsteps" = "blue",
      "Calories Burned" = "red"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Daily Footsteps and Calories Burned",
    x = "Daily Value",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```





# boxplot of calories burned

# boxplot of calories burned and footsteps


```{r}
# Combine both variables
box_data <- data.frame(
  Value = c(data$Footsteps, data$Calories_Burned),
  Variable = rep(
    c("Daily Footsteps", "Calories Burned"),
    each = nrow(data)
  )
)

# Create horizontal boxplots with separate scales
ggplot(box_data, aes(x = Value, y = Variable, fill = Variable)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.4,
    color = "black",
    outlier.size = 3
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
  limits = c("Calories Burned", "Daily Footsteps")
) +
   
  scale_x_continuous(
  breaks = seq(0, 8000, by = 500)
)+
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 8000))+
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Daily Footsteps" = "blue",
      "Calories Burned" = "red"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot Distribution of Daily Footsteps and Calories Burned",
    x = "Daily Value",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    
  )
```

# statistical analysis 
```{r}
# Perform simple linear regression
model <- lm(Calories_Burned ~ Footsteps, data = data)

# Get regression results
results <- summary(model)

# Create statistical results table
stat_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c(
    "Number of observations",
    "Regression intercept",
    "Regression slope",
    "Correlation coefficient (r)",
    "R-squared (R²)",
    "P-value",
    "Significance level"
  ),
  Result = c(
    nobs(model),
    coef(model)[1],
    coef(model)[2],
    cor(data$Footsteps, data$Calories_Burned,
        use = "complete.obs"),
    results$r.squared,
    results$coefficients[2, 4],
    0.05
  )
)

# Round results to 4 decimal places
stat_table$Result <- round(stat_table$Result, 4)

# Display table
knitr::kable(
  stat_table,
  caption = "Simple Linear Regression Results"
)

```
# equation of the line 

```{r}
# Perform simple linear regression
model <- lm(Calories_Burned ~ Footsteps, data = data)

# Get intercept and slope
intercept <- coef(model)[1]
slope <- coef(model)[2]

# Create regression equation
equation <- paste0(
  "Calories Burned = ",
  round(intercept, 2),
  ifelse(slope >= 0, " + ", " - "),
  abs(round(slope, 4)),
  " * Footsteps"
)

# Display equation
cat(equation)

```

# statistic summary 

```{r}
# Calculate summary statistics
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c(
    "Number_of_Observations (days)",
    "Average_footsteps",
    "Average_calories_burned",
    "Range_footsteps",
    "Range_calories_burned",
    "SD_footsteps",
    "SD_calories_burned"
  ),

  Result = c(
    sum(complete.cases(data[, c("Footsteps", "Calories_Burned")])),
    mean(data$Footsteps, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(data$Calories_Burned, na.rm = TRUE),
    diff(range(data$Footsteps, na.rm = TRUE)),
    diff(range(data$Calories_Burned, na.rm = TRUE)),
    sd(data$Footsteps, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd(data$Calories_Burned, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

# Round results to 2 decimal places
summary_table$Result <- round(summary_table$Result, 2)

# Display summary statistics table
knitr::kable(
  summary_table,
  caption = "Summary Statistics of Daily Footsteps and Calories Burned"
)
```
